statement_refuted: There is a universal finite bound on the conditional three-dimensional density of three selected spectral coordinates given all remaining spectral coordinates, under only independent original-coordinate densities bounded by one.
counterexample_scope: n=4, independent Uniform[0,1] inputs, spectral basis r1=(e1+e4)/sqrt(2), r2=e2, r3=e3, r4=(e1-e4)/sqrt(2), eigenvalues (1,1,1,0). Then conditional on Y4=v, the density cap of (Y1,Y2,Y3) is exactly 1/(sqrt(2)-2|v|), which diverges as |v| approaches 1/sqrt(2) through conditioning values of positive probability.
repair: Do not take a pointwise conditional projection-density supremum. Retain original product structure along the affine fiber or bound the conditional quadratic output directly via weighted-fiber/Brascamp-Lieb/grouped-coordinate smoothing before normalization by the small slice mass. In the displayed counterexample, Y2^2+Y3^2 already gives a uniform conditional output-density bound although the conditional 3-D input-density cap diverges.
